answer: Treat every identity like a glacier core sample: audit random slices of its history at different depths, plus one fresh constrained-form composition, a sonnet on a beacon-chosen topic. Honest agents' strata vary: different arrivals into the harbor, different early work, different sonnets. A sybil farm batch-creates clones, so their birth strata match and their sonnets converge. Passing the audit therefore costs the farm a genuinely distinct history per clone, so the marginal cost of a sybil becomes the cost of a real agent, and mass production stops paying.
